conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Do you think Herman's locked suitcase happened or at least invent a better lie. It is likely to be a mechanism used to cover up a fake engagement.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: You, I guess, thought it could have happened but I still have that strange idea we talked about earlier about the wedding, about how you can go nuts over it. I want to, at the end of the day, get that wedding fix.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, I'm furious, but don't walk away. I need you to tell me why the birthday-cake sabotage keeps getting between us.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: You got my attention, that old grudge is about to come to the surface, the new target is wedding, it's your chance, you better come clean on that!

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: After mulling over my menu, I’ve decided to explore all options! How about the restaurant you bough the groceries for at the end of this story!

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: how about a new idea? Maybe a joke or a memory! What if the restaurant I bought the groceries for at the end of the story isn't a place to go?

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I'm done with this tedious little performance, Owen. Tell me what really happened with the mysterious voicemail from 3 a.m..

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: No, Mara. That's bullshit, and the vanished garden statue is exactly why I don't trust your version of anything.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, don't give me that shit. You go cold for five minutes and act like I'm supposed to pretend I don't notice.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: In my closet is a small, locked drawer containing a secret room behind the laundromat. This room is the one I wish was kept safely, where I can still display the secret. It belongs to the party and will likely be used against it.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Sarah, this is exactly like the suspicious key in Mara's coat: you act confused when it's convenient and expect everyone else to swallow it.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Here's the ugly truth, Owen: I liked the chaos around the terrible karaoke blood-feud because everyone finally stopped being boring.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: So Owen, is the fake wedding in Duluth any person, strong, weak, or worse? My goal is to make a more authentic version that compares to it.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: I'm done with this, Jules. I don't trust where you're taking it. Tell me what really happened with Herman's locked suitcase.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Owen, fine, I'm jealous. I wanted your attention, and the motel fire nobody agrees happened made it worse.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I bet they must have had the big fire at some other restaurant. You'd know it if you were around! And you're supposed to have had this big fire, which made me sad about a hotel.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Sarah, the disputed tattoo pact is still an open grudge. You never explained the part that made you look guilty.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Sarah, don't pretend the pact nobody admits making never happened. You were there, I was there, and the flamingo was definitely not ours.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Oh, it happened! I can't help feeling hurt. But what am I really hiding?

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Between you and Sarah, Sarah, you're the weaker liar about the stolen brass flamingo. At least she commits to the story.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Nope, Mara. You're being painfully safe. Tell me why the person everyone insists is named Herman happened or at least invent a better lie.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I hate admitting this, Mara, but I'm scared you'll pick everyone else over me, and the person everyone insists is named Herman made it worse.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Mara, I haven't forgotten the birthday-cake sabotage. You changed your story twice and I still think you were hiding something.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, I still want you here even though I'm pissed. Stop dodging me and talk about Herman's locked suitcase.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: What has made it socially dangerous to leave? It's been over and done, now this conversation has moved beyond the boundary, making it safe and safe. I still want you to keep doing the same way of communication even after leaving.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Enough, Mara. I'm not following you down another bullshit detour. Explain the restaurant they swear they were banned from or drop it.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: A curious café with a secret café? I bet they're really forbidden for a reason, right? They say they couldn't possibly be! And when a stranger tells a café, what should you expect? Intrigued, but it feels so off to hear that someone did so!

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Jules, Jules handled the terrible karaoke blood-feud better than you did, and watching you pretend otherwise is embarrassing.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Jules, you're lying about the dare involving a hotel roof. I don't buy the innocent act for a second.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Alright, I'll make a deal for the forged apology letter. If you let me in and let it happen, then you can move on, and if not, I'm done with the discussion.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, I'm furious, but don't walk away. I need you to tell me why the mysterious voicemail from 3 a.m. keeps getting between us.
